line_in_post: The biggest group of Indian adults looks 'fine' on the scale — but not inside.
finding: 43.3% of Indian adults are 'metabolically obese' even though their BMI is under 25.
verbatim_quote: In this nationally representative study of India, we show that (i) the largest proportion (43.3%) of the population in India is metabolically obese but with BMI<25 kg/m2 (referred to as MONO), (ii) MONO is more prevalent in rural areas and among males, (iii) MOO showed highest risk for diabetes and CAD, while MONO showed the highest risk of CKD especially among females.
paper: High prevalence of metabolic obesity in India: The ICMR-INDIAB national study (ICMR-INDIAB-23)
